critical_steps: The full two-vector family has an invertible frame operator.
After deleting the first vector, the singleton {e1} is exactly a Parseval K-frame.
The source operator I-S_J^{-1}S_I is nevertheless singular.
In the published restriction it does not preserve R(K).
The exact condition is the defining inequality S_rem >= a K K*, equivalently Douglas range inclusion.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional scalar g-frame specialization and positive-operator characterization.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made about unrelated approximate-dual propositions or about an indexed erratum being impossible.

scientific_limitations: The finding concerns the redundancy equivalence theorem, not the approximate-dual results of the paper.
The corrected operator inequality is exact for the erased-family question but no attempt is made to optimize every quantitative bound printed in the source.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same two-vector counterexample.
title: An inverse-frame-operator erasure test is too strong for \(K\)-\(g\)-frames
